summaries.field: financial econometrics / time series volatility modeling
summaries.information_need: A researcher wants to specify a volatility model whose current variance depends on both past shocks and its own past values, and to know the parameter restrictions that keep such a process well-behaved (stationary, finite unconditional variance).

summaries.field: financial econometrics / time series volatility modeling
summaries.information_need: A researcher wants a formal derivation showing that a stated restriction on the model's coefficients is both necessary and sufficient for the process to be stationary, with finite, well-defined unconditional variance and zero autocovariance across distinct time points, a property needed before applying the model to real data.

summaries.field: financial econometrics / time series volatility modeling
summaries.information_need: A researcher wants to know what conditions on the model parameters guarantee that higher-order moments (beyond variance) of the process exist, and how the resulting distribution's tail heaviness can be characterized, since heavier-than-normal tails matter for assessing risk in the modeled series.

summaries.field: time series volatility modeling / persistence measures
summaries.information_need: A researcher wants a way to summarize how long a shock's effect persists in the conditional variance equation, a single interpretable measure of the typical delay before its influence dissipates, useful for comparing how quickly different fitted models forget past shocks.

A practitioner wants to estimate a regression model whose error variance follows a volatility process, and needs the likelihood-based estimator, its score and information-matrix structure, and a practical iterative algorithm to compute it along with its asymptotic distribution.

An analyst wants to know how the autocorrelation and partial autocorrelation functions of the squared series behave under this class of volatility models, so they can be used in practice to identify appropriate lag orders and check adequacy from sample data.

A practitioner wants a formal statistical test for whether time-varying volatility is present in a regression model's errors, along with a clear understanding of when such a test breaks down or fails to distinguish reliably between competing lag specifications for the same alternative.

An analyst wants to compare competing volatility specifications for a macroeconomic time series, judging fit through residual diagnostics, tail-shape statistics, and the width of forecast intervals across calm and turbulent periods, to see whether the added flexibility of a richer specification is empirically worthwhile relative to a simpler one.
